messages:
Maya: heads-up — during a 24h soak with long-context Llama-4 tests we see steady RSS growth on a subset of hosts, not explained by retained requests.
Jonathan: can you paste the perf dump? is this allocation or fragmentation? :thinking:
Maya: initial profiler points to kv_cache arena: free space exists but effective usable memory decreasing. Suspect fragmentation and allocator fit choice.
Sasha: re-ran with heap sampling. here's the short snapshot:
Sasha: ```
# kv cache stats
total_slots: 1_536_000
allocated_bytes: 38_416_000_000
free_bytes: 4_192_000_000
largest_free_block: 64_000_000
avg_free_run: 12_400
fragmentation_ratio: 0.109
most_common_block_size: 3_072
``` 
Eli: interesting that largest_free_block is only 64MB while avg free run is tiny — suggests lots of small holes between live KV segments.
Maya: exact workload is long open-ended generation with repeating prefixes; KV entries get appended then reused/shrunk. allocator current policy is best-fit within bucketed power-of-two size classes with 3 probe passes.
Jonathan: we have three hypotheses: (1) too coarse block sizes (internal fragmentation), (2) allocation churn causing interleaved small free slots (external frag), (3) reclamation heuristics not coalescing quickly enough.
Sasha: proposed micro-proto: introduce a background "sweeper" that coalesces adjacent free slots and trims trailing free slabs when host under low load. Sweeper runs with max 100ms CPU per 10s window.
Maya: also prototyping an "adaptive-fit" where small hot allocations are packed into slablets inside a larger superblock — reduces inter-slot gaps. It trades CPU for memory compaction.
InfraBot: perf-regression-alert: host-id i-0a3f spike in rss +12% over baseline at 2620000000.
Eli: can we test 2 variants: (A) sweeper-only, (B) sweeper + adaptive-fit packing. Run 8h soak with same seed.
Maya: I kicked off both in canary fleet (8 nodes each). Quick microbench after 1h:
Maya: ```
variant A (sweeper-only): rss delta -4.7% vs baseline, p95 latency +0.3ms
variant B (sweeper+pack): rss delta -11.2% vs baseline, p95 latency +1.1ms
cpu overhead B: +6% steady
``` 
Jonathan: impressive on memory. Latency regression in B is small but possibly visible for tail-sensitive routes.
Sasha: more detail — fragmentation estimator went from 0.109 -> 0.042 on B. That aligns with reclaimed small holes.
Eli: concerns: B's packer requires more locking and reorganizing KV index entries — need to ensure no regressions under high QPS.
Maya: plan: run extended soak (48h) on staging with traffic mix, enable packer only on lower-tier routes and monitor p99. If stable, rollout phased to production with 5% increments.
Jonathan: also add metrics: compact_ops/sec, bytes_compacted, compaction_cpu_ms. Add alert if p99 increases >5% or error rate +0.1%.
Sasha: implementation notes: keep packing idempotent and safe across crashes — use transient tombstones for moved segments and switch pointer atomically.
Maya: patch in review at #pr/kv-adaptive-fit. Main questions in review: tuning of superblock size (currently 8MB) and sweep cadence.
Eli: suggestion: make sweep cadence auto-scale by observing freed-bytes/sec; lower cadence when allocation churn high to avoid thrashing.
Jonathan: ok. Action items:
- Maya: finish 48h soak and post final numbers (ETA +2d)
- Sasha: add compaction metrics and crash-safety doc (ETA +1d)
- Eli: run high-QPS failure-mode test for packer (ETA +3d)
- InfraBot: scheduled canary rollout to production if soak passes
Maya: thanks — ping me if you want raw perf traces (I uploaded them to s3://redwood-test/kv-frag/2620000123). :thumbsup:
InfraBot: deployment-notice: started canary for variant B on group canary-2 at 2620000300.
